theCommittedCaptionsWereDecidedUnderAnIn.correctionToFix140: The fabricated ruler was not a HALF em on this form. Per-glyph advances under the old code measure ~1002 mils against the font's true 384-696: 'Nebraska S' 100.2 pt where the font gives 45.92, 'urt F' 50.1 against 19.22, a single space 10.0 against 2.5. The old walker charged 500 mils per BYTE of a two-byte code, i.e. a full em per visible glyph, roughly 2.0x to 2.6x too wide. Captions were measured as reaching about twice as far to the right as they actually print.
theCommittedCaptionsWereDecidedUnderAnIn.whyThatDecidesWhetherNECanBeRebuilt: Caption harvesting decides which printed words are within reach of a widget, and the court-owned vs participant-owned role classification is derived from that. Systematically doubling every caption's width makes captions appear to reach widgets they do not reach. Rolling the module back to unblock the rebuild would restore that. Rebuilding on the current module is what refuses. So the family cannot honestly be rebuilt until the Type0 width path is repaired by a lane that holds the corpus -- and this lane's measurement above says that repair may be width-only, which makes it a smaller job than FIX140 concluded.
